title: ISO 45001:2018
source: ISO 45001:2018, clauses 4 to 10 (reference numbers and official short titles)
licence: Reference numbers with the official short titles only; not the text of the standard. Purpose, guidance, audit questions and typical evidence are our own words. Buy the standard for the requirements.

requirements.title: Clause 4 · Context of the organization
requirements.purpose: Grounds the OH&S system in the real conditions people work in, the needs of workers and others, and a clear scope.

requirements.title: Understanding the organization and its context
requirements.purpose: Builds the OH&S system around the real conditions in which your people work and the outside forces that shape their health and safety.
requirements.guidance: Record the internal and external issues that bear on OH&S results: legislation and enforcement, the labour market and use of agency workers, contractors and subcontracting, shift patterns, home and lone working, an ageing workforce, new technology, financial pressure and workplace culture. Include how workers are represented, for example through trade unions or safety representatives. A short dated PESTLE or SWOT with an owner is enough for a small company. Say how each issue is handled, for example in the risk register or an objective. Typical findings are a context list copied from the quality system with nothing about the workforce, and one never revisited after a restructuring or a new site. Since the 2024 amendment, also decide and record whether climate change is a relevant issue for you, and keep the reasoning even when the answer is no.
questions: Which internal and external issues affect your ability to prevent work-related injury and ill health?
How did workforce issues such as agency labour, shift work or remote work shape the system?
How did these issues feed into your risks, opportunities and objectives?
When was the context last reviewed and what changed?
Have you decided whether climate change is a relevant issue, and where is that decision recorded?
evidence: Dated context analysis (PESTLE, SWOT or similar) with owner
Workforce profile, for example contract types, shifts and work locations
Cross-reference from issues to the risk register or objectives
Management review minutes showing the context was reviewed

requirements.title: Understanding the needs and expectations of workers and other interested parties
requirements.purpose: Identifies who has a stake in your health and safety and which of their needs become requirements.
requirements.guidance: List workers, contractors, regulators, customers, insurers, emergency services and neighbours, and write what each needs. Decide which become legal or other requirements. Review it regularly and after changes. A common finding is a list that leaves out agency workers or contractors, or that does not feed the legal register. Since the 2024 amendment, note where interested parties have climate-related expectations, such as customer or lender reporting requests.
questions: Who are your interested parties and what do they need?
Which needs have you taken on as requirements?
How are workers' needs identified?
When was the list last reviewed?

requirements.title: Determining the scope of the OH&S management system
requirements.purpose: Fixes the boundary of the OH&S system so that every activity under your control or influence that can affect health and safety is covered.
requirements.guidance: Write a short scope naming the sites, activities, products and services covered. Base it on your context, the needs of workers and other parties, and your planned work activities, including work done at client sites, by mobile and home workers and by contractors on your premises. Everything inside the boundary that can affect OH&S performance must be covered. Certification bodies challenge scopes that leave out higher-risk work, such as maintenance, installation or field service, to make the system look simpler. Keep the scope as documented information and check that it matches the certificate.
questions: Which sites, activities and work locations does the scope cover?
How are work at client sites, home working and contractors on your premises treated?
Why is any activity outside the scope, and is it higher risk?
Does the scope match the certificate and what happens day to day?
evidence: Approved scope statement with version and date
List of sites and work locations, including off-site work
Rationale for any activity left outside the scope

requirements.title: OH&S management system
requirements.purpose: Requires a working OH&S management system whose processes are planned, linked and improved, drawing on what you learned about context and workers' needs.
requirements.guidance: Show the processes that make up the system and how they connect: worker consultation and participation, hazard identification and risk assessment, legal requirements, operational controls, management of change, contractor control, emergency response, incident investigation, monitoring, internal audit and management review. A process map or table with owners, inputs, outputs and records is enough. Build OH&S into existing business processes such as purchasing, design and HR rather than keeping it in a separate safety file. Common findings are a manual describing processes that do not happen, no working process for worker participation and the whole system held by one safety adviser.
questions: Which processes make up your OH&S system and who owns each?
How are OH&S requirements built into purchasing, design and HR processes?
How did your context and workers' needs shape the processes?
What did you change in the system after the last review or incident?
evidence: Process map or register with owners, inputs and outputs
Records showing processes run and are monitored
Change log showing the system was improved

requirements.title: Clause 5 · Leadership and worker participation
requirements.purpose: Makes top management accountable for preventing injury and ill health and gives workers a real say in how health and safety is run.

requirements.title: Leadership and commitment
requirements.purpose: Makes top management personally accountable for preventing work-related injury and ill health, and for a culture in which people can speak up safely.
requirements.guidance: Top management should own the prevention of injury and ill health and the provision of safe and healthy workplaces, not hand it to the safety adviser. Look for visible behaviour: safety walks, leading reviews of serious incidents, approving resources and making sure OH&S fits business plans. Leaders must also make sure worker consultation and participation work in practice, support the safety committee, and protect workers from reprisal when they report incidents, hazards, risks or opportunities. Auditors interview leaders on the main risks, recent incidents and what they did about them, and ask workers whether reporting feels safe. Typical findings are leaders who cannot name the top risks, no real protection against reprisal and safety owned by one person.
questions: What are your highest OH&S risks and what have you personally done about them?
How do you make sure workers can report hazards and incidents without fear of reprisal?
How do you support the safety committee or worker representatives?
How are OH&S resources decided and approved?
evidence: Records of leadership safety walks or tours
Board or management minutes reviewing OH&S performance
Policy or procedure protecting workers who report from reprisal

requirements.title: OH&S policy
requirements.purpose: Sets out top management's commitment to safe and healthy work in a short statement that fits the nature of your OH&S risks and frames the objectives.
requirements.guidance: Write a short policy that reflects your actual work and risks. Alongside the core commitments (safe and healthy working conditions that prevent injury and ill health, fulfilling legal and other requirements, eliminating hazards and reducing OH&S risks, continual improvement, and consulting and involving workers and, where they exist, their representatives), make it specific to the hazards you manage. It should give a frame for the OH&S objectives. Top management signs and dates it, it is communicated to workers in a form they understand and it is available to interested parties. Findings include template text unrelated to the risks, a missing commitment to worker consultation and staff who cannot say what the policy means for them.
questions: Who approved the policy, when, and when was it last reviewed?
How does the policy reflect the specific OH&S risks of your work?
Where does it commit to hazard elimination and to worker consultation and participation?
How is it communicated to workers, including those with limited language or literacy?
evidence: Policy displayed at workplaces or published
Induction or briefing records covering the policy

requirements.title: Organizational roles, responsibilities and authorities
requirements.purpose: Makes sure OH&S duties have named owners with authority at every level, including someone who reports OH&S performance to top management.
requirements.guidance: Assign responsibilities for the OH&S system and for key duties: risk assessment, permits to work, first aid, fire wardens, contractor control, inspections and statutory examinations. Make clear that managers and supervisors own safety in their areas and that every worker takes responsibility for the parts of the system they control. One role must be responsible for conformity of the system and for reporting OH&S performance to top management. Record this in job descriptions or a RACI table and keep it current. Typical findings are supervisors unaware of their safety duties, appointed first aiders who have left and authority to stop work that exists only on paper.
questions: What OH&S responsibilities do supervisors and workers have, and do they know them?
Who reports OH&S performance to top management and how often?
Who can stop unsafe work, and has it happened?
How are vacant safety roles such as first aiders and fire wardens covered?
evidence: Role descriptions or RACI matrix covering OH&S duties
Appointment records for first aiders, fire wardens and competent persons
OH&S performance reports to top management

requirements.title: Consultation and participation of workers
requirements.purpose: Gives workers at all levels, especially non-managerial staff, a real say in decisions about their health and safety and an active part in the work of the system.
requirements.guidance: Set up channels that suit your size: a safety committee, elected or appointed representatives, toolbox talks, surveys and hazard reporting routes. Give the time, training, information and resources needed for real participation, and remove barriers such as language, literacy, fear of reprisal or lost pay for meeting time. Treat consultation (asking for views before a decision, for example on the policy, objectives, contractor controls and the audit programme) separately from participation (involving workers in the work itself, such as hazard identification, risk assessment, choosing controls, training needs and incident investigation). Put the emphasis on non-managerial workers. National law may add duties on worker representation and consultation. Findings include committees with no shop-floor members, consultation after decisions are made and investigations done without workers.
questions: How do non-managerial workers take part in hazard identification and incident investigation?
Which decisions were workers consulted on before they were taken in the last year?
What barriers to participation did you find and how did you remove them?
Show a change that came from worker input.
evidence: Safety committee terms of reference and minutes showing worker members
Worker representative appointment and training records
Consultation records on the policy, objectives or contractor controls
Risk assessments or investigation reports showing worker involvement
Survey results and the responses to them

requirements.title: Clause 6 · Planning
requirements.purpose: Plans how hazards, OH&S risks, legal requirements and opportunities are dealt with and sets measurable OH&S objectives.

requirements.title: Actions to address risks and opportunities
requirements.purpose: Covers the planning work that links context, hazards, OH&S risks, legal requirements and opportunities to concrete actions.
requirements.guidance: This parent asks whether OH&S planning is joined up. Hazard identification, risk assessments, the legal register and the risk and opportunity register should feed one action plan, and the actions should appear in objectives, controls, training and emergency arrangements. Planned changes, permanent or temporary, should be brought into planning too. Auditors check the sub-clauses in detail and use this one to see whether the parts connect.
questions: How do hazard identification, the legal register and the risk registers feed one action plan?
How are planned changes brought into OH&S planning?
Show an action that started from a risk assessment and where it ended up.

requirements.title: Actions to address risks and opportunities: general
requirements.purpose: Combines context, workers' needs, hazards and legal requirements to find the OH&S risks and opportunities you need to act on, including those from planned change.
requirements.guidance: Use the outputs of 4.1, 4.2, hazard identification and the legal register to list OH&S risks and opportunities, and also risks and opportunities for the system itself, such as losing a key competent person or a chance to improve consultation. Consider potential emergency situations and planned changes, whether permanent or temporary, such as a new production line, a reorganisation or a peak season. Record the risks and opportunities and the processes used. Common findings are a risk register copied from the quality system, risks to the system itself missing and no link to change.
questions: Which OH&S risks and opportunities did you identify, and from which inputs?
Which risks and opportunities relate to the OH&S system itself?
How did planned changes feed the assessment?
What actions followed and how is their effect checked?

requirements.title: Hazard identification and assessment of risks and opportunities
requirements.purpose: Finds the ways work can harm people, physically and mentally, assesses the risks and spots opportunities to make work safer and healthier.
requirements.guidance: Run hazard identification as a continuing, proactive process, not a one-off exercise. Look at how work is organised and at social factors (workload, hours, harassment and bullying), leadership and culture, routine and non-routine tasks, equipment, materials and layout, product design, human factors, past incidents, emergencies and new knowledge. Cover everyone affected: employees, agency workers, contractors, visitors and people near or away from your sites. Assess OH&S risks with a defined method and criteria, and assess risks to the system as well. Look for OH&S opportunities, such as adapting work to workers or removing a hazard during a refit. Involve workers. Findings include generic assessments, psychosocial hazards ignored, non-routine work missed and reviews only after injuries.
questions: How do you identify hazards in non-routine work such as maintenance, cleaning and breakdowns?
How are psychosocial hazards such as workload, working hours and harassment identified and assessed?
What method and criteria are used to assess OH&S risk, and are they applied consistently?
How were workers involved in the last risk assessment you completed?
Which OH&S opportunities have you identified and acted on?
evidence: Hazard register and task or activity risk assessments
Documented risk assessment method and criteria
Psychosocial or work-related stress risk assessment
Records of worker involvement in assessments
Review dates and triggers, such as change or incident

requirements.title: Determination of legal requirements and other requirements
requirements.purpose: Ensures you know which health and safety laws and adopted requirements apply, how they apply to your work, and that this knowledge stays current.
requirements.guidance: Build a register of OH&S legal requirements: the national laws that implement the EU framework and individual directives relevant to you (workplaces, work equipment, manual handling, display screens, chemical agents, noise and so on), statutory inspections and examinations, plus collective agreements, client site rules and industry codes you have adopted. For each, note how it applies, who owns it and when it was last checked. Use a reliable update service, tell workers about relevant changes and review the register on a set cycle. Auditors find registers that list laws without saying how they apply, statutory examinations missing and no evidence of review.
questions: How do you find out about new or changed OH&S law?
Show how one requirement applies to a specific task and who owns it.
Which other requirements, such as client rules or collective agreements, have you adopted?
How are relevant changes communicated to workers?
evidence: Legal and other requirements register with applicability and owners

requirements.title: Planning action
requirements.purpose: Converts risks, requirements and opportunities into actions built into how you work.
requirements.guidance: Plan actions for hazards, risks, legal duties and emergencies. State how they fit into processes and how you will evaluate them. Consider the hierarchy of control, technology and financial needs, and the views of workers. Findings are actions not integrated and no effectiveness checks.
questions: What actions come from risks and legal duties?
How are they built into processes?
How do you check effectiveness?
How did workers contribute?
evidence: Action plan with owners and dates

requirements.title: OH&S objectives and planning to achieve them
requirements.purpose: Covers setting OH&S objectives and planning how to achieve them.
requirements.guidance: This parent asks whether OH&S objectives drive real improvement. Objectives should come from the policy, risk assessments, legal requirements and worker consultation, and each should have a plan with an owner, resources, dates and indicators. Auditors check the sub-clauses in detail and use this one to see whether objectives are tracked and reported to management and workers.
questions: Which OH&S objectives did you set this year and which risks, legal duties or worker concerns led to each?
How are workers told about progress against the objectives?
What happens when an OH&S objective falls behind plan?

requirements.title: OH&S objectives
requirements.purpose: Sets measurable targets that support the policy and improve safety and health.
requirements.guidance: Set objectives consistent with the policy, taking into account risks, legal duties and the views of workers. Make them measurable where practical, monitored and communicated. Examples include reducing manual handling injuries or completing inspections. Findings include vague objectives, no owner and no tracking.
questions: What are your objectives and why?
How are they measured?
How did workers take part?
Who owns each?

requirements.title: Planning to achieve OH&S objectives
requirements.purpose: Defines, for each OH&S objective, the actions, owner, resources, deadline and indicators used to judge progress.
requirements.guidance: For each objective write the actions, who is responsible, the resources, the dates and how results will be evaluated, using indicators that show progress. Mix leading indicators, such as inspections completed, near misses reported or training delivered, with lagging ones such as lost-time injuries. Build the actions into business processes such as budgets, purchasing and maintenance. Review progress regularly. Findings are plans without budgets or dates, and objectives measured only by injury rates, which can discourage reporting.
questions: For one objective, what actions, owner, resources and dates are planned?
Which leading and lagging indicators track progress?
How are the actions built into budgets and business processes?
How often is progress reviewed and by whom?
evidence: Objective action plans with owners, resources and dates

requirements.title: Clause 7 · Support
requirements.purpose: Provides the resources, competence, awareness, communication and records that safe and healthy work depends on.

requirements.title: Resources
requirements.purpose: Makes sure the OH&S system has the people, time, money, equipment and infrastructure it needs.
requirements.guidance: Identify what the system needs: competent OH&S advice, time for worker representatives and the safety committee, occupational health services, first aid provision, protective equipment, guarding and other engineering controls, statutory inspections and maintenance, and training. Tie resources to risk assessment outputs, objectives and management review actions, and record the decisions. Auditors look for controls from risk assessments that were never funded, statutory inspections overdue for lack of budget and representatives with no time for their role.
questions: How do you decide what resources the OH&S system needs?
Which risk controls were delayed for lack of time or money?
What time and resources do worker representatives have?
Who approves OH&S spend?
evidence: Occupational health and first aid arrangements

requirements.title: Competence
requirements.purpose: Ensures workers have the competence to work safely and to recognise hazards, and that people in OH&S roles can carry them out.
requirements.guidance: For each role, state the OH&S knowledge, skills and experience needed, including the ability to recognise hazards in their own work. Cover roles with specific duties: supervisors, permit issuers, first aiders, fire wardens, plant and vehicle operators, risk assessors and worker representatives. Close gaps through training, supervision or recruitment, check that it worked, and keep records, including licences and certificates with expiry dates. Include agency workers and contractors. Common findings are lapsed certificates for licensed equipment, no check that training was effective and agency staff working before induction.
questions: What OH&S competence does each role need, and how was it decided?
How do you check that workers can recognise the hazards in their own work?
How do you track licences and certificates that expire?
How do you confirm agency workers and contractors are competent?
evidence: Training records and certificates with expiry dates
Agency worker and contractor competence records

requirements.title: Awareness
requirements.purpose: Makes sure workers know the policy, their hazards, the lessons from incidents, their part in the system and their right to remove themselves from serious danger.
requirements.guidance: Workers should know the OH&S policy and objectives, how they contribute and what happens if they do not follow the system. They should also know the hazards and risks in their own work, what was learned from investigations of incidents relevant to them, and that they can withdraw from a work situation they reasonably believe poses imminent and serious danger without being penalised for it. Cover employees, agency workers, contractors and visitors as relevant. Use induction, toolbox talks and safety alerts, and test awareness by asking people. Findings include workers unaware of their right to stop work, incident lessons not shared and awareness limited to the policy.
questions: What would you do if asked to carry out a task you believed was seriously dangerous?
What are the main hazards in your job and how are they controlled?
What did you learn from the last incident in your area?
How are agency workers, contractors and visitors made aware?
evidence: Induction content covering hazards, the right to stop work and the policy
Toolbox talk and safety alert records

requirements.title: Communication
requirements.purpose: Covers how OH&S information is planned, shared with workers and exchanged with outside parties, taking account of workforce diversity.
requirements.guidance: This parent asks whether OH&S communication reaches everyone who needs it and runs both ways. Plan what is communicated, to whom, when and how, consider language, literacy, culture and disability, and take account of legal requirements. Make sure workers' views are heard and outside parties such as contractors and authorities are included. Auditors check the sub-clauses in detail and use this one to see whether messages actually land.
questions: How is OH&S communication planned and who owns it?
How do you reach workers with different languages or literacy levels?
How do workers' concerns reach decision makers?
evidence: Sample communications in the languages used on site

requirements.title: Communication: general
requirements.purpose: Sets up planned OH&S communication that suits the diversity of your workforce and meets legal requirements.
requirements.guidance: Build a matrix of subject, audience, timing, method and owner. Take account of diversity, such as gender, language, culture, literacy and disability, for example by translating key safety information or using pictograms. Include communications required by law, such as safety signs, hazard information and accident reporting, and consider the views of outside parties. Make sure the information is consistent with the system and reliable, and keep evidence of key communications. Findings are safety information in one language only, shift workers missed and no record of what was communicated.
questions: What OH&S information do you communicate, to whom and when?
How do you adapt communication for language, literacy or disability?
Which communications are required by law?
How do you check that the plan works?

requirements.title: Internal communication
requirements.purpose: Ensures OH&S information reaches workers at all levels, shifts and locations, and lets them contribute to improvement.
requirements.guidance: Share OH&S performance, incident lessons, changes to risk assessments and changes to the system across levels, functions, shifts and sites, including with contractors and visitors on site. Use toolbox talks, briefings, noticeboards and messaging. Give workers simple ways to raise hazards and ideas, such as near-miss cards or an app, and show that each gets a response. Weaknesses are one-way messaging, night shifts never briefed and near-miss reports with no feedback.
questions: How do workers on all shifts hear about incidents and changes?
How can workers raise hazards and ideas, and how quickly do they get a response?
How is information passed to contractors and visitors on site?
Show a worker suggestion that led to a change.
evidence: Toolbox talk and briefing records by shift
Near-miss or hazard report log with responses

requirements.title: External communication
requirements.purpose: Makes sure required and planned OH&S communication with outside parties is accurate, timely and recorded.
requirements.guidance: Decide who speaks for the company on OH&S and who reports to the authorities. Meet statutory duties to notify certain accidents, dangerous occurrences and occupational diseases to the enforcing authority within the time limits set by national law. Exchange safety information with contractors, clients on shared sites, occupational health providers and emergency services. Log enquiries and inspector visits and your responses. Weak spots are late or missing accident notifications, no record of inspector advice and contractors not told about site hazards.
questions: Which incidents must you notify to the authorities and how do you meet the deadlines?
Show a recent notification or inspector visit and your response.
How do you exchange hazard information with clients and contractors on shared sites?
Who may speak for the company on OH&S matters?
evidence: Accident and occupational disease notification records
Information exchanged with contractors and clients

requirements.title: Documented information
requirements.purpose: Covers which OH&S documents and records you keep and how they are created, approved and controlled.
requirements.guidance: This parent asks whether OH&S documentation is proportionate, usable by workers and controlled. Keep what the standard and the law require and what you need to work safely, such as risk assessments, safe systems of work, inspection records and training records. Make sure current versions are where the work is done and that records are kept as long as required. Auditors check the sub-clauses in detail and use this one to see whether documents support safe work.
questions: Which risk assessments, safe systems of work and statutory records does the system depend on?
How are OH&S documents kept current and records retained for the periods the law sets?
Can workers find the current safe system of work at the job?

requirements.title: Documented information: general
requirements.purpose: Defines the OH&S documents and records the system needs: those the standard and the law require plus those you need to work safely.
requirements.guidance: Map the items the standard expects you to hold, among them the scope, policy, roles, the risk and opportunity processes and results, the hazard identification and risk assessment method, legal and other requirements, objectives, enough on operational controls and emergency arrangements to show they run as planned, monitoring and calibration results, compliance evaluation, audit and management review results, incidents and corrective actions, and evidence of competence and communication. Add records the law requires, such as statutory examinations, exposure monitoring and health surveillance. Record where each item lives. Findings are an undocumented risk assessment method, missing compliance evaluation records and procedures nobody uses.
questions: Show where each required OH&S record is kept.
Which records does the law require you to keep?
How did you decide how much to document beyond the minimum?
Can workers find the current version quickly?
evidence: Map of required documented information to locations
Sample statutory records, such as examinations and exposure monitoring

requirements.title: Creating and updating
requirements.purpose: Makes sure OH&S documents are identifiable, approved and in a format workers can use.
requirements.guidance: Give each document a title, version, date and owner, and an approval step before release. Write safe systems of work and method statements so the people doing the job can use them: plain words, pictures, the right language, and available at the point of work. Involve workers in reviewing the procedures they use. Review after incidents, changes and legal updates. Findings usually involve no evidence of approval, risk assessments not updated after a change and documents workers cannot read.
questions: How are OH&S documents approved before use?
How do you make procedures usable by workers with different languages or literacy levels?
Were workers involved in writing or reviewing the procedures they use?
What triggers a review of a risk assessment or procedure?
evidence: Approved documents with version, date and approver
Safe systems of work in suitable languages or formats
Change history after incidents or changes

requirements.title: Control of documented information
requirements.purpose: Ensures the right OH&S documents are available where work is done and that records, including health data, are protected and kept as long as required.
requirements.guidance: Control distribution, access, storage, change, retention and disposal. Make sure current risk assessments and procedures are at the point of work and obsolete ones are removed. In line with 5.4, give workers and their representatives timely access to the documented information that concerns them. Protect health surveillance and occupational health records as special category personal data under the GDPR, limit access to those who need it, and keep exposure and health records for the periods national law sets, which can be long. Control external documents such as safety data sheets and manufacturer instructions. Findings are old risk assessments in use, health records on shared drives and missing safety data sheets.
questions: How do you make sure workers use the current procedure?
How can workers and representatives access the documents that concern them?
Who can access health surveillance records and how are they protected?
How long do you keep exposure and health records, and why?
evidence: Master document list including safety data sheets
Retention schedule citing legal periods for exposure and health records

requirements.title: Clause 8 · Operation
requirements.purpose: Controls day-to-day work through the hierarchy of controls, management of change, procurement and contractor controls, and emergency planning.

requirements.title: Operational planning and control
requirements.purpose: Covers how everyday work is controlled: operational controls, hazard elimination, management of change, procurement, contractors and outsourcing.
requirements.guidance: This parent asks whether risk assessment outputs turn into controls that work on the ground. Controls should follow the hierarchy of controls, changes should be assessed before they happen, and purchasing, contractors and outsourced work should be brought under control. Auditors check the sub-clauses and spend most of their time on site watching work, so evidence here is largely observation backed by records.
questions: Which work activities need operational controls?
How do you check that controls are followed on the ground?
How are changes, contractors and outsourced work controlled?
evidence: Safe systems of work and permits to work

requirements.title: Setting up operational controls
requirements.purpose: Establishes the controls needed to keep work safe and healthy and to meet legal requirements, including coordination with other employers on shared sites.
requirements.guidance: Set criteria and controls for work linked to significant OH&S risks: safe systems of work, permits for high-risk tasks such as hot work, confined spaces and work at height, isolation and lock-out, maintenance and inspection. Adapt work to workers, for example through ergonomic workstations, rest breaks and job rotation. Keep enough records to show work is done as planned. Where several employers share a workplace, agree with the others who controls what, and coordinate rules and emergency arrangements. Findings include procedures not followed on the floor, non-routine work done without a permit and no coordination with other employers on site.
questions: Which tasks require a permit to work or a written safe system of work?
How do supervisors check that controls are followed?
How have you adapted work to workers, for example for ergonomics or shift work?
How do you coordinate with other employers on shared sites?
evidence: Safe systems of work and completed permits
Coordination agreements or meeting records with other employers

requirements.title: Eliminating hazards and reducing OH&S risks
requirements.purpose: Requires controls chosen by the hierarchy of controls, removing hazards first and relying on protective equipment only as a last resort.
requirements.guidance: For each significant risk, work down the hierarchy: eliminate the hazard, substitute something less hazardous, use engineering controls and reorganise the work, use administrative controls including training, and only then provide protective equipment. Several layers are often combined. Record why a higher control was not reasonably practicable and revisit the decision when technology or circumstances change. Involve workers in choosing controls, as they know what will work. Check that controls are effective through inspection, exposure monitoring or observation. Findings are risk assessments that jump straight to protective equipment and training, no record of why elimination was rejected and equipment issued without fit testing or training.
questions: Show a hazard you eliminated or substituted in the last year.
For a risk controlled mainly by protective equipment, why were higher controls not practicable?
How were workers involved in choosing the controls?
How do you check that engineering controls and protective equipment remain effective?
evidence: Risk assessments showing controls ranked by the hierarchy
Records of elimination or substitution projects
Engineering control inspection or test records
Protective equipment selection, fit testing and issue records

requirements.title: Management of change
requirements.purpose: Ensures changes to work, equipment or people do not introduce uncontrolled hazards.
requirements.guidance: Define which changes need review, such as new equipment, materials, layouts, staffing, legal updates and knowledge, then assess risk before they go ahead. Record approvals and communicate. Review the consequences of unplanned changes. Findings are changes made without risk review and no record.
questions: How do you decide what counts as a change?
Show a recent change and its risk review.
How are workers told?
How are unintended changes reviewed?

requirements.title: Procurement
requirements.purpose: Controls the OH&S risks that come with buying goods and services, using contractors and outsourcing work.
requirements.guidance: Purchasing: specify OH&S requirements before buying equipment, substances and services, and check them on arrival, for example CE marking, safety data sheets and installation checks. Contractors: set selection criteria that include OH&S, check competence and insurance, share hazard information both ways, induct them, agree controls and monitor their work; consider the risks your work creates for them, theirs for your workers and theirs for others. Outsourcing: keep control of outsourced functions and processes and define the type and extent of control in the contract. Findings are contractors working without induction or permits, equipment bought without a safety review and no monitoring of contractor performance.
questions: What OH&S criteria do you use to select and approve contractors?
How do you exchange hazard information with contractors before work starts?
How do you monitor contractor safety performance on site?
What OH&S checks are made before new equipment or substances are used?
How is the OH&S side of outsourced work controlled?
evidence: Contractor induction and permit to work records
Contractor monitoring or site inspection records
Purchase specifications and equipment acceptance checks

requirements.title: Emergency preparedness and response
requirements.purpose: Prepares you to protect workers, contractors and visitors in realistic emergencies, with first aid, evacuation and links to emergency services.
requirements.guidance: Work out which emergencies are credible, such as fire, serious injury, chemical release, structural failure or violence, and prepare a response for each with first aid, evacuation, escalation and external services. Take account of the needs and abilities of the people involved, for example visitors, lone workers and people with disabilities who may need a personal evacuation plan. Train people, run drills at suitable intervals, include contractors and visitors, and share relevant information with emergency services and neighbours where needed. Review plans after drills and real events. Typical findings are drills that do not involve all shifts, out-of-date first aid cover and plans that ignore visitors, contractors and people who need help to evacuate.
questions: Which emergencies have you planned for and how did you decide they were credible?
When did you last run a drill, on which shift and with whom?
How are first aiders and fire wardens trained and replaced when they leave?
How are visitors, contractors and people who need help to evacuate included?
evidence: First aid provision and training records

requirements.title: Clause 9 · Performance evaluation
requirements.purpose: Monitors OH&S performance, checks legal compliance, and audits and reviews the system with input from workers.

requirements.title: Monitoring, measurement, analysis and performance evaluation
requirements.purpose: Covers how you monitor OH&S performance and evaluate compliance with legal and other requirements.
requirements.guidance: This parent asks whether OH&S data is collected, trusted and used. Monitor controls, hazards, legal compliance and objectives with leading and lagging indicators, keep equipment calibrated, and report results to management and workers. Auditors check the sub-clauses in detail and use this one to see whether data leads to action.
questions: Which leading and lagging OH&S measures do you rely on?
How do you confirm that legal OH&S requirements are being met?
How are OH&S results shared with management, workers and their representatives?

requirements.title: Monitoring, measurement, analysis and performance evaluation: general
requirements.purpose: Ensures you monitor the OH&S measures that matter, with reliable equipment, and use the results to judge OH&S performance.
requirements.guidance: Decide what to monitor: how far legal requirements are met, activities linked to hazards and risks, progress on objectives and how well controls work. Set the method, frequency, criteria and responsibility. Use a balance of leading indicators (inspections, near-miss reporting, training completion) and lagging ones (injuries, ill health, lost time). Calibrate or verify equipment such as noise meters, gas detectors and air samplers. Analyse trends and share results with workers. Auditors look for injury rates as the only measure, data never analysed and uncalibrated monitoring equipment.
questions: Which leading and lagging indicators do you track and why?
How do you monitor exposure to noise, dust or chemicals where relevant?
How do you make sure monitoring equipment is reliable?
Show a decision taken because of the data.

requirements.title: Evaluation of compliance
requirements.purpose: Checks at set intervals that each OH&S legal and other requirement is met and acts on any gap.
requirements.guidance: Decide how often to evaluate each requirement, based on risk and how often it changes. Use site inspections, record checks and audits by a competent person, and cover statutory duties such as examinations of lifting equipment and pressure systems, fire safety arrangements, exposure limits and health surveillance. Record the result for each requirement, any gaps and the actions, and keep management aware of compliance status. Common findings are a legal register with no evaluation records, overdue statutory examinations and evaluation only before certification.
questions: How often is each legal requirement evaluated and how was this decided?
Show the latest compliance evaluation and the resulting actions.
How do you track statutory examinations and inspections?
Who performs the evaluation and how are they competent?

requirements.title: Internal audit
requirements.purpose: Covers your own audits of whether the OH&S system conforms and works.
requirements.guidance: This parent asks whether internal audits are credible. Plan audits across the system with more weight on higher-risk work, use competent and impartial auditors, report results to management and to workers and their representatives, and close the actions. Auditors check the sub-clauses in detail and use this one to see whether your audits find real issues.
questions: How are high-risk activities and contractor work covered by the audit cycle?
How are audit results reported to workers and their representatives?
How quickly are OH&S audit findings closed, and who checks?

requirements.title: Internal audit: general
requirements.purpose: Checks at planned intervals that the OH&S system meets your own and the standard's requirements and works where the work is done.
requirements.guidance: Audit every part of the system and every site over the cycle, against the standard, your procedures and legal requirements. Spend time on site observing work, talking to workers and checking permits and controls, not only reviewing documents. Use competent auditors who do not audit their own work. Report results to the relevant managers and to workers and their representatives. Common findings are desk-only audits, high-risk tasks never audited and repeat findings.
questions: What scope and criteria did the last audit use?
How much of the audit involved observing work and talking to workers?
How do you ensure auditor competence and impartiality?
How were the results shared with workers and representatives?
evidence: Audit reports with scope and criteria

requirements.title: Internal audit programme
requirements.purpose: Plans the audit programme, weighting it by OH&S risk, past results and worker input, and makes sure results reach workers.
requirements.guidance: Set the frequency, methods, responsibilities, consultation, reporting and scope. Weight the programme by risk, so high-risk activities, contractor work and areas with incidents are audited more often. Consult workers on the programme, and report results to the relevant workers, their representatives and other relevant parties. Update the programme after incidents and changes. Frequent findings are programmes that treat all areas equally, missed audits and results never shared with workers.
questions: How did OH&S risk and incident history shape audit frequency?
How were workers consulted on the programme?
Were all planned audits completed and, if not, why?
How are audit results communicated to workers and representatives?
evidence: Communication of audit results to workers

requirements.title: Management review
requirements.purpose: Has top management step back at planned intervals, decide whether the OH&S system is suitable, adequate and effective, and share the outcome with workers.
requirements.guidance: Prepare a review pack that gives top management the full picture: where earlier actions stand, what has changed in the context, legal requirements and risks, progress on objectives, trends in incidents and nonconformities, monitoring and compliance results, audit findings, what came out of worker consultation and participation, whether resources are adequate, communications from outside parties and ideas for improvement. Top management takes part and records decisions on the system, objectives, resources, integration with business processes and improvement. Share the relevant outcomes with workers and their representatives. Typical findings are reviews missing incident trends or consultation outcomes, no recorded decisions and nothing shared with workers.
questions: Which inputs were covered at the last review and which were missing?
How were the outcomes of worker consultation considered?
What decisions came out on objectives and resources?
How were the outcomes communicated to workers?
evidence: Performance and incident reports used as inputs
Action list with owners and closure

requirements.title: Clause 10 · Improvement
requirements.purpose: Learns from incidents and nonconformities and improves OH&S performance and culture over time.

requirements.title: Improvement: general
requirements.purpose: Makes you actively look for ways to improve OH&S performance and act on them.
requirements.guidance: Use incident and near-miss trends, inspections, audits, monitoring, worker suggestions and review decisions to find improvements, such as removing a hazard at source, better equipment or redesigned tasks. Plan and track them as actions with owners and check the effect on risk. Findings occur when improvement only follows injuries or when worker suggestions are not tracked.
questions: Where do OH&S improvement ideas come from?
Show a recent improvement and its effect on risk.
How are worker suggestions tracked and answered?
evidence: OH&S improvement log with the risk reduction achieved
Worker suggestion and near-miss records leading to change

requirements.title: Incident, nonconformity and corrective action
requirements.purpose: Makes sure incidents and nonconformities are dealt with, investigated with workers and fixed at root cause using the hierarchy of controls.
requirements.guidance: React promptly to incidents, near misses and nonconformities: make the area safe, give first aid and deal with the consequences. Investigate with the workers involved and other relevant parties to find root causes, including organisational factors, and check whether similar situations exist elsewhere. Review existing risk assessments, assess any new or changed hazards before acting and choose corrective actions using the hierarchy of controls. Verify effectiveness, notify the authorities where the law requires, update the system and share lessons with workers. Keep records. Findings include blame-focused investigations, near misses not reported, actions limited to retraining and no verification.
questions: Show a recent incident investigation and how workers took part.
How did you identify root causes beyond individual error?
How did the corrective action follow the hierarchy of controls?
How did you check the action worked and share the lessons?
evidence: Investigation reports with root cause analysis
Corrective action log with effectiveness checks

requirements.title: Continual improvement
requirements.purpose: Ensures OH&S performance, the system and the safety culture get better over time, with workers involved and informed.
requirements.guidance: Show improving trends in OH&S measures, such as fewer high-potential incidents, better exposure results or more near-miss reporting, backed by closed actions and review decisions. Promote a culture that supports the system, encourage workers to take part in improvement and tell them about the results. Auditors look for evidence over several periods and are wary of claims based only on falling injury numbers, which can reflect under-reporting.
questions: How have key OH&S measures changed over recent years?
How do you know falling injury numbers are not due to under-reporting?
How do workers take part in continual improvement?
How are improvement results communicated to workers?
evidence: Trend charts of leading and lagging indicators
